newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN BREWERS TO RAISE BEER PRICES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN BREWERS TO RAISE BEER PRICES.

text.p: Bulgarian beer producers said on Friday they would raise beer prices from September because of high energy charges and barley prices.

"We are forced to raise beer prices in September because of high electricity and water charges and high prices of brewery barley from this year's crop", Petar Paunkov, chairman of the Beer Producers' Union, told a news conference.
He declined to say by how much prices would rise.

"Poor quality of the Bulgarian barley production is a major problem for the beer producers but we expect to meet our annual needs of 100,000-110,000 tonnes of brewery barley from local production," Paunkov said.
"Bulgaria's total brewery and feed barley output this year is seen at some 500-600,000 tonnes," he added.
Bulgaria's barley output stood at 450,000 tonnes last year and at 1.172 million tonnes in 1995.
Beer producers have secured some 40-50 percent of their annual needs already and are buying the barley at $110-120 per tonne ex-works, Paunkov said.
Beer producers had to import some 20,000 tonnes of brewery barley at $125-135 per tonne delivered in the country this spring to cover a consumption gap until this year's crop.

"Beer producers are planning to offer futures contracts to cash strapped barley producers in a move to secure next year's crop and boost barley quality," Paunkov said. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
